name: Close
verdict: Self-serve to build and test inside your own Close organization, but other organizations can connect only after Close reviews the app: click Make Public and submit it. No review timeline is published.
needGuide: Yes: the build is short, but Close's review decides when customers outside your organization can connect.

auth.detail: Likely: authorization-code flow (app.close.com/oauth2/authorize, token at api.close.com/oauth2/token) with offline_access for refresh tokens and a one-hour access token. Unverified this session.

approval.gate: Mandatory review before other organizations can connect. OAuth apps are private by default: only members of your own Close organization can authorize them. To open the app up, click Make Public in its settings and submit it for review; Close replies by email, and once approved any Close user can authorize it. No review timeline is published. A listing in the Close Integrations Directory is separate and optional: once the app is public, email support@close.com to apply (public OAuth 2.0 integrations only).

scopes.why: Likely coarse scopes (all.full_access, offline_access); behaviour follows the authorizing user's permissions (unverified).
scopes.summary: Likely coarse scopes (all.full_access, offline_access) rather than per-object permissions; behaviour follows the authorizing user's permissions. Unverified.

cost: Free to register; Close plans are paid, but API access is believed to be included
prerequisites: Account and owner: A Close organization admin is likely needed to create OAuth apps; use a company-owned Close account (a trial can serve).
Where you register: Close → Settings → Developer → OAuth Apps → Create App. The app is private to your own Close organization until Close approves it.
Cost: Free to register; Close plans are paid, but API access is believed to be included

registerAt.path: Close → Settings → Developer → OAuth Apps → Create App. The app is private to your own Close organization until Close approves it.

steps.do: Create a Close trial org with a company email
In Settings → Developer → OAuth Apps, click Create App, enter the app details and redirect URIs, then copy the Client ID and Client Secret
Implement authorization-code flow requesting offline_access plus the needed scope
Store refresh token; refresh access tokens before expiry
Test with API calls on leads, contacts and activities; handle rate-limit headers
Click Make Public and submit the app for Close's review; customers outside your organization can connect only after Close approves it by email

roles.team: A Close organization admin is likely needed to create OAuth apps; use a company-owned Close account (a trial can serve).
roles.customer: The user authorizing grants access as themselves; organization admins may restrict who can authorize or install apps (unverified).

testing: A Close trial organization acts as the test tenant; there is no separate sandbox that I know of.

blockers.problem: Other organizations can't authorize the app until Close approves it
blockers.fix: Submit it for review as soon as the flow works.
Pitch least-privilege at the user-role level.
Reconnect if the authorizing user leaves.

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth client and refresh logic, draft the review submission and the directory application email, and run test calls.
automation.humanMust: Create the app in the Close UI, submit it for Close's review, and have the customer user authorize.

uncertain: The registration path and the review that makes an app public were confirmed in Close's developer docs on 30 Oct 2026.
Scope names, token lifetime, the review's criteria and its timeline were not confirmed.
